- When sentiment is negative and forecast drops sharply, model tends to underestimate true price — correct by adding 1–2% to forecasted lows.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment, model often overcorrects downward — adjust forecast by +1–3% to avoid premature reversal.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model underestimates true price — apply upward bias of 0.5–1.5% to compensate for mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon — especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — add 0.5–1.5% to first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to capture momentum — increase forecast by 1–2% in first 3–5 days of sentiment shift.
- Model tends to overestimate price in late 30-day horizon when sentiment is negative — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for last 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed, model often averages out — use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher weight to recent sentiment if >0.10, lower if < -0.20.
